title: 6.28.3 Lab: Pick a piece and step
description: Red and black take turns: click one of your pieces to pick it up, click a square one step diagonally forward to move it, and every rule lives in moveKind.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: This is your board from 6.27.4. The pieces are there, but a click does nothing.

steps.title: Whose turn, and what is picked
steps.instructions: Below `let grid;`, add `let turn = 'r';`, `let picked = null;` and `let message = '';`. In `newGame()`, after `grid = makeBoard();`, set `turn = 'r';`, `picked = null;` and `message = "Red's turn: click a piece";`. Below `colorOf`, add the two helpers from the reading: `function nameOf(t) { return t === 'r' ? 'Red' : 'Black'; }` and `onBoard(r, c)`. In `drawTop()`, show the message instead of the count: `text(message, 10, 22, 16, 'white');`.
hints: If you brought your 6.27.4 work forward, your names may differ; keep yours.
You can leave `countPieces` in: nothing calls it now, and day four can use it.

steps.title: Pick up your own piece
steps.instructions: Write `clickAt(x, y)` above `drawPieces`: `const c = floor(x / CELL);`, `const r = floor((y - TOP) / CELL);`, then `if (!onBoard(r, c)) return;` and `const p = grid[r][c];`. If `p !== '' && colorOf(p) === turn`, set `picked = { r: r, c: c };` and `return;`. In `draw()`, before `drawBoard();`, add `if (mouse.presses()) clickAt(mouse.x, mouse.y);`. At the end of `drawBoard()`, light the picked square: `if (picked !== null) { fill('rgba(255, 215, 0, 0.45)'); rect(picked.c * CELL, TOP + picked.r * CELL, CELL, CELL); }`. Run: click a red piece and it lights; a black one does not.
hints: Take `TOP` off `y` before dividing, or every click lands one row too low.
`onBoard` comes first: a click in the strip at the top is row -1, and `grid[-1]` does not exist.

steps.title: One rule function
steps.instructions: Below `onBoard`, write `moveKind(fr, fc, tr, tc)` from the reading: off the board, not your piece, or not onto an empty square answers `''`; then `const dr = tr - fr;`, `const dc = tc - fc;`, not diagonal answers `''`, not forward answers `''` (`const ahead = turn === 'r' ? dr < 0 : dr > 0;`), and `abs(dr) === 1` answers `'step'`; anything else answers `''`. Then `function isLegal(fr, fc, tr, tc) { return moveKind(fr, fc, tr, tc) !== ''; }`.
hints: Red moves up the screen, so its row number gets smaller: `dr < 0`.
Nothing calls these yet, so Run looks the same. The next step uses them.

steps.title: Move, and pass the turn
steps.instructions: Write `doMove(fr, fc, tr, tc)` from the reading: copy the letter to the new square, empty the old one, set `picked = null;`, pass the turn with `turn = turn === 'r' ? 'b' : 'r';` and set `message = nameOf(turn) + "'s turn";`. At the end of `clickAt`, `if (picked !== null && isLegal(picked.r, picked.c, r, c)) doMove(picked.r, picked.c, r, c);`. Run and play a few moves each: red, then black, then red.
hints: Try a step backward, a step sideways and a step onto another piece: none of them moves.
Clicking a different piece of your own picks that one up instead.

requirements.title: A click becomes a row and a column
requirements.description: The click is turned into a row and a column with floor, taking the strip at the top off first. Help: 6.28.1 (Reading: From a click to a square, and one rule function)

requirements.title: You pick up your own piece
requirements.description: A click on a piece whose colour matches the turn remembers it as the picked piece. Help: 6.28.1 (Reading: From a click to a square, and one rule function)
requirements.hint: if (p !== '' && colorOf(p) === turn) picked = { r: r, c: c };

requirements.title: One square diagonally
requirements.description: A step is one row and one column away, tested with abs or another way. Help: 6.28.1 (Reading: From a click to a square, and one rule function)

requirements.title: Forward only, by colour
requirements.description: Red moves up the screen and black moves down: the direction depends on whose turn it is. Help: 6.28.1 (Reading: From a click to a square, and one rule function)

requirements.title: The turn passes
requirements.description: After a move, the turn goes to the other player: red to black, black to red. Help: 6.28.1 (Reading: From a click to a square, and one rule function)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Pick a piece and step". The task: turn a click into a row and a column with floor (taking TOP off y), pick up a piece whose colour matches the turn, and write one rule function, moveKind, that answers 'step' only for a move one square diagonally forward (up for red, down for black) onto an empty square; isLegal asks it, and doMove moves the letter, clears the picked piece and passes the turn. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries, nested ifs, switch statements and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.
